question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated authority within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced through successive anti-corruption campaigns that sidelined potential rivals in the military and senior ranks, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus against his removal before the end of 2026. With no designated successor in place and generational turnover norms already set aside after his third term, the 21st Party Congress scheduled for 2027 is positioned as the likely setting for a fourth term rather than a leadership transition. Ongoing public appearances, policy continuity through mid-2026, and stable elite alignment reflect this positioning. Nevertheless, abrupt health developments, major economic disruptions, or unexpected fractures within party institutions remain low-probability pathways that could still alter the outcome ahead of the congress.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom holds a narrow lead in the 2028 Democratic presidential nominee market, but the top three outcomes remain tightly bunched because no major candidate has declared and the field stays highly fragmented two years before primaries begin. Newsom’s earlier advantage has narrowed amid ongoing scrutiny of his California record on budgets, housing, and migration. Late declarations or polling shifts before formal contests could still reorder the field.
